# Full Blog Api With Relations

Build a complete blog REST API using Prisma ORM and Express.js with SQLite.

The project is at `/home/user/myproject`. Node.js and Express are pre-installed.

Define the following schema with migrations:
- `User`: id, email (unique), name
- `Post`: id, title, content (optional), published Boolean @default(false), authorId (FK to User), createdAt DateTime @default(now())
- `Comment`: id, body, postId (FK to Post), authorId (FK to User)

Build an Express server at `server.js` on port 3000 with these endpoints:
- `POST /users` — create user
- `GET /users/:id/posts` — get published posts by user (include comment count)
- `POST /posts` — create post (body: `{ title, content, authorId }`)
- `PATCH /posts/:id/publish` — set `published: true`
- `POST /posts/:id/comments` — add a comment (body: `{ body, authorId }`)
- `GET /posts/:id` — get post with author and comments included

Start the server: `node server.js`
Port: 3000

input.result:
Built a complete blog REST API with Prisma ORM + Express.js on SQLite.

## What was done

**1. Prisma schema** (`prisma/schema.prisma`) — defined three models with full relations:
- `User`: id, email (unique), name + relations to posts & comments
- `Post`: id, title, content (optional), published (@default(false)), authorId (FK), createdAt (@default(now())) + comments relation
- `Comment`: id, body, postId (FK), authorId (FK)

**2. Migration** — ran `prisma migrate dev --name init`, creating `prisma/migrations/20260703054209_init/migration.sql` and the SQLite `dev.db`.

**3. Prisma Client** — generated the client. Note: this project uses **Prisma 7.8**, which removed the legacy Rust engine and requires a **driver adapter** for the query-compiler engine. Installed `@prisma/adapter-better-sqlite3` + `better-sqlite3`, and the client is instantiated as:
```js
const adapter = new PrismaBetterSqlite3({ url: dbPath });
const prisma = new PrismaClient({ adapter });
```

**4. Express server** (`server.js`, port 3000) with all endpoints:
| Endpoint | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `POST /users` | create user (email, name) |
| `GET /users/:id/posts` | published posts by user, each with `_count.comments` |
| `POST /posts` | create post `{ title, content, authorId }` |
| `PATCH /posts/:id/publish` | set `published: true` |
| `POST /posts/:id/comments` | add comment `{ body, authorId }` |
| `GET /posts/:id` | post with author + comments (incl. comment authors) |

## Verification
All endpoints were tested end-to-end (create user → create post → publish → add comment → fetch post with relations → list published posts with comment count). The published-filter was confirmed to exclude unpublished drafts.

The server is currently running in the background on port 3000. Start it anytime with:
```
node server.js
```
